title: Track every ticket, stay honest, measure your work

say: Track every ticket, stay honest, and measure your work.
This is the video for module 3 of Online Customer Support.
A ticket is simply a record of one customer request, from the moment it arrives until it is closed. A free Google Sheet can do this job.

say: Give each ticket a number, and write the real time it was received.

panel.heading: Key columns in your ticket sheet

say: Note the customer's first name and the channel, so you can find the chat again.

panel.heading: Key columns in your ticket sheet

say: Choose a category, like delivery or wrong item, and a priority. Use dropdown lists so everyone types the same words.

panel.heading: Key columns in your ticket sheet

say: Record your first reply time and the status: New, Waiting for customer, Waiting for us, or Resolved.

panel.heading: Key columns in your ticket sheet

say: Finally, the resolved time and a short note of what happened. Every evening, filter for Waiting for us and set reminders.
Protect the sheet. Share it only with colleagues who need it, and never store bank details or ID numbers in it.

say: High priority means money taken but no goods, any safety issue, or a customer who has already chased twice. For example, Ruth logs a customer who paid 23,000 naira two days ago with no delivery. She chases dispatch at once.

General questions, feedback, requests for future products.

say: If a customer reports a skin reaction, illness after food, or a shock from a device, treat it as High priority.

say: Customers trust a business that keeps its word. So do not promise what you cannot control, do not hide known problems, and never make up a reason.

panel.heading: Honest support, every time
right: I will update you by 2 pm

say: Say the courier estimates Thursday. Tell waiting customers about a delay before they chase you. And when you do not know, say: I will find out and update you by 2 pm.

say: First response time is how long customers wait for the first human reply. Ada logs 5 tickets. The waits are 7, 25, 6, 48 and 14 minutes.

panel.heading: First response time, worked out
items: For each ticket: first reply minus time received
Divide by the number of tickets

say: Added together, that is 100 minutes.

say: Divide by 5 tickets, and her average is 20 minutes.

say: An average can hide problems. One ticket waited 48 minutes, while Ada was in a meeting. So she plans to check chats between meetings.

say: Resolution rate is resolved tickets divided by tickets received, times 100. Ada resolved 72 of 80, so 90%.

cards.d: 45 solved in the first reply, out of 72 resolved.
34 customers gave 4 or 5, out of 40 responses.

say: First contact resolution is the share solved in the first reply. 45 of 72 gives 62.5%.

cards.d: 45 solved in the first reply, out of 72 resolved.
34 customers gave 4 or 5, out of 40 responses.

say: CSAT, customer satisfaction, is happy ratings divided by all responses. 34 of 40 gave 4 or 5, so 85%. Always say how many customers answered.
And never close tickets too quickly just to raise a number. That lowers satisfaction.

say: To remember. Log every request as a ticket. Money and safety come first. For any harm, advise stopping use and escalate at once.
Build your FAQs from your most common categories. And end every half-page weekly report with one action.

say: Your turn. Build your tracker and log at least 10 tickets. Write a one-page policy, three FAQ answers and three escalation levels. Then calculate your metrics and write a half-page report with one action.
